title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
gist: Seychelles' Marie-May Jeremie argues that Western Indian Ocean conservation requires cross-border financing because species and ecosystems ignore national boundaries, and urges governments at the Nairobi Convention COP12 to authorize a government-led next phase for a Western Indian Ocean Regional Conservation Trust Fund (RCTF) that complements national funds and development banks.

insights.claim: Sea turtles nesting in northern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, migrate through the Mozambique Channel and the wider Indian Ocean, showing that national action alone cannot protect migratory species across their full range.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Illustrates why conservation outcomes depend on regional rather than national financing and governance.
insights.quote: South Africa can protect their nesting beaches, but no country alone can protect their entire journey.

insights.claim: Protecting migratory species, interconnected habitats and shared ecosystems requires countries to cooperate, and the finance supporting that cooperation must be able to cross borders as well.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Argues for pooled regional financing vehicles rather than project-by-project national grants.
insights.quote: the finance supporting such cooperation must be capable of making the same journey as the turtle
insights.locator: The turtle embodies the central challenge

themes.theme: Economic stakes of Western Indian Ocean ecosystems

insights.claim: About 60 million people live within 100 km of the Western Indian Ocean coastline, and healthy marine ecosystems underpin their food security, livelihoods, trade, tourism and storm protection.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Ecosystem degradation directly threatens regional blue-economy sectors such as fisheries and tourism.

insights.claim: The region's mangroves and seagrasses store carbon, its reefs sustain biodiversity and its waters support migratory species, so protecting them is in the rest of the world's interest, not just the region's.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Frames the case for international donor and blue-carbon finance contributions to regional conservation.
insights.locator: But their value also reaches far

themes.theme: Seychelles model and regional governance mandate

insights.claim: Seychelles' experience with marine spatial planning and conservation finance shows that ocean protection can be integrated into national development when ambitious goals are backed by political commitment and innovative finance, and other Western Indian Ocean countries are pursuing similar strategies.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Positions Seychelles' conservation-finance approach as a replicable template for the region.
insights.locator: Regional leaders do not lack ambition

insights.claim: Through the Nairobi Convention and its Regional Ocean Governance Strategy, governments have a mandate for stronger ocean cooperation; the remaining task is creating financing mechanisms capable of delivering it.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Identifies financing, not political mandate, as the binding constraint on regional ocean governance.
insights.quote: The Regional Ocean Governance Strategy has established the mandate, and we are all now tasked with creating the financing mechanisms capable of delivering it.

insights.claim: Meeting the goal of protecting 30% of marine and coastal areas by 2030 requires more than drawing boundaries: protected areas need science, management, enforcement, community participation and investment in sustainable livelihoods.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Suggests 'paper parks' without sustained funding will fail, raising the long-term financing need behind 30x30 pledges.
insights.quote: Achieving the common objective of protecting 30% of marine and coastal areas by 2030 requires more than drawing boundaries on a map.

insights.claim: With the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction now in force, new possibilities are opening for conservation beyond national waters, and the Western Indian Ocean region must be ready to influence its implementation.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: The high-seas treaty's entry into force creates a new governance arena where regional blocs will compete to shape rules.

insights.claim: Conservation requires continuity because reefs and fisheries do not recover on project deadlines or funding cycles, making short-term project grants poorly suited to the task.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Argues for endowment-style or trust-fund financing over time-limited project finance.
insights.quote: Reefs do not recover according to project deadlines, just as fisheries won’t be replenished in sync with funding cycles.

insights.claim: Women from three coastal villages in Anjouan, Comoros, after learning from fishing communities in Madagascar and Zanzibar, temporarily closed part of their reef to octopus fishing; on reopening, the average octopus caught was twice its previous weight.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that temporary closures can sharply raise fishery yields, and that knowledge transfer across borders spreads effective practice.

themes.theme: Western Indian Ocean Regional Conservation Trust Fund

insights.claim: Governments are working toward a Western Indian Ocean Regional Conservation Trust Fund (RCTF) to mobilize sustained finance for cross-border conservation priorities, designed to complement rather than compete with national funds, development banks and project finance.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: A new regional pooled-finance vehicle could become a channel for donor and blended conservation capital in the region.
insights.quote: the RCTF will focus only where cross-border cooperation adds clear value
insights.locator: Nonetheless, governments are working toward a

insights.claim: No single fund can finance the whole conservation agenda; pollution controls, greener ports and other maritime priorities require different instruments.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Implies a layered financing architecture with distinct instruments for distinct maritime needs, including port decarbonization.
insights.locator: No single fund can finance every

insights.claim: The RCTF's next phase must be government-led to set its priorities, safeguards, governance structure and relationship with existing institutions, while international partners are asked to help build a regionally owned financing architecture rather than another isolated project.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: Signals a shift toward regional ownership of conservation finance, changing how donors engage.
insights.quote: The real opportunity is to invest in the region’s own capacity to lead the effort.

insights.claim: At the Twelfth Conference of the Parties to the Nairobi Convention (COP12), marking 40 years of cooperation, governments should authorize a government-led next phase for the RCTF.
insights.speaker: MARIE-MAY JEREMIE
insights.so_what: COP12 is a near-term catalyst to watch for formal launch of the regional trust fund.
